Mark Pavliuk

★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Remodeling Contractors Serving Vancouver, Portland & Southwest Washington

Most homeowners do not start a remodel because they want construction in their house. They start because the kitchen no longer works, the bathroom feels outdated, the home needs more space, or the layout has stopped fitting the way their family lives. JDI Construction helps homeowners across Portland, Vancouver, and Southwest Washington turn frustrating spaces into homes that feel easier, warmer, and better planned.

We are a family-owned remodeling company based in downtown Vancouver, serving the Portland-Vancouver metro since 2007. Our team handles kitchen remodels, bathroom remodels, whole-home renovations, additions, ADUs, and exterior remodeling with careful planning, skilled crews, and clear communication from the first conversation through the final walkthrough.

With nearly two decades of local experience, hundreds of verified homeowner reviews, and licensed work across Washington and Oregon, JDI is built for projects where the details, timeline, and accountability matter.

Full-Service Home Remodeling, Managed Under One Roof

A good remodel is more than new finishes. It takes planning, permits, scheduling, trade coordination, and clean execution on site. JDI manages the full process so you are not left juggling designers, carpenters, electricians, plumbers, and inspectors on your own.

Kitchen Remodeling

Your kitchen should work for everyday life, not just look good in photos. We design and build kitchens with better layouts, smarter storage, quality cabinetry, durable countertops, improved lighting, and finishes that fit the character of your home.

Bathroom Remodeling

A good bathroom should feel calm, clean, and easy to use every day. We remodel hall baths, guest baths, primary suites, and accessibility-friendly bathrooms with walk-in showers, custom tile, better lighting, improved storage, and layouts that make the room feel larger and more comfortable.

Whole-Home Renovations

Older homes in Portland and Vancouver often need more than one room updated. We handle whole-home renovations that improve flow, update finishes, modernize systems, and bring the home together with one cohesive plan.

Home Additions

When you need more space, we design and build additions that feel like they belong. That can include expanded kitchens, new bedrooms, larger living areas, second-story additions, guest suites, and home offices.

ADUs & Accessory Dwelling Units

ADUs can create space for family, rental income, guests, or a private workspace. JDI helps homeowners navigate layout, zoning, permitting, and construction so the finished unit is useful, code-compliant, and built to last.

Exterior Remodeling

The Pacific Northwest is hard on homes. We also handle exterior remodeling, including siding, decking, windows, and outdoor improvements that help protect your home while improving curb appeal.

Why Homeowners Choose JDI Construction

Remodeling is personal. You are letting a contractor into your home, your budget, and your daily routine. That is why the way a project is managed matters just as much as the finished result.

We plan before we build: Scope, budget, timeline, materials, permits, and site logistics are worked through before construction starts.
We know Northwest homes: Older framing, wet weather, basement moisture, tight lots, and previous remodel work all affect how a project should be built.
You get one accountable team: Your project is managed by people who know the work, not handed from one disconnected crew to another.
We communicate like adults: Clear updates, realistic timelines, and honest conversations when something needs to change.
We build for daily life: The finished space has to work for cooking, cleaning, kids, guests, pets, storage, and the way your household actually moves.
We have a real local reputation: Since 2007, JDI has earned hundreds of reviews from homeowners across Vancouver, Portland, and nearby communities.

We are a good fit for homeowners who want the project thought through before anyone starts tearing into walls. If you care about layout, finish quality, communication, and having one team accountable for the work, that is where JDI does its best work.

Our Remodeling Process

Our process is built to remove guesswork. Before construction starts, we want you to understand the scope, the budget, the timeline, and what life at home will look like while the work is happening.

Consultation: We talk through your goals, your home, your budget, and what is not working in the current space.
Planning: We help shape the scope, layout, materials, and project priorities.
Proposal: You receive a clear estimate with the project scope, expected timeline, and major selections outlined.
Permits & Scheduling: When permits are required, we handle the process and coordinate the construction schedule.
Construction: Our team manages the jobsite, the trades, the inspections, and the details that make the remodel come together.
Final Walkthrough: We review the finished work with you and address final details before the project is complete.
Remodeling That Fits the Way Northwest Homes Are Built

Homes in Portland, Vancouver, and Southwest Washington come with real quirks: older framing, tight lots, wet winters, aging electrical, basement moisture, and previous remodel work hidden behind the walls. A good remodeler plans around those realities before they turn into expensive surprises.

That local experience matters whether we are opening up a kitchen in a Portland bungalow, remodeling a bathroom in Vancouver, adding an ADU in Camas, or updating an exterior that takes on rain for half the year. The right plan protects your budget, your timeline, and your home.

Mark Pavliuk
Portland, OR · Sep 2026
View on Google
★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Where Craftsmanship Meets Care

At JDI Construction, every remodel starts with a conversation around a kitchen table, not a contract. We're a family-owned remodeling company headquartered in downtown Vancouver, Washington, and since 2007 we've helped Pacific Northwest homeowners reimagine the spaces they spend their lives in.

The "JDI" in our name stands for "Just Dream It," but for us it has always meant something more: do the work right the first time. That mindset is why we've earned a 4.9-star average across 223+ verified Google reviews, and why families come back to us project after project.

Our Story

JDI Construction was founded in 2007 by Alex Kulchitskiy, who wanted to do remodeling differently. The idea was simple: treat every home like it's your own family's, give homeowners honest timelines instead of optimistic ones, and refuse to leave a site until the work is right. The referrals followed.

Since 2007 and more than 500 projects later, what began as a one-truck operation in Portland has grown into one of Southwest Washington's most trusted full-service remodelers. Our headquarters now sits at 1419 Broadway Street in downtown Vancouver, with designers, carpenters, electricians, tile setters, and project managers working under one roof.

The JDI Approach: Experience That Shows Up on Site

Remodeling in the same region since 2007 teaches you a few things. We've seen what survives Cascadia winters and what doesn't. We know which permits the City of Vancouver actually reads, and how to lay out a Portland bungalow kitchen so it works for the next thirty years of family meals.

Every project is led by a dedicated project manager and built by our in-house crews. Our teams handle the full residential scope (design, demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, finish carpentry, tile, paint, and final cleanup), so there are fewer hand-offs and one point of contact when you have a question.

What We Build

JDI Construction is a true full-service remodeler. The projects we live and breathe:

The neighborhoods we work in are the ones our kids go to school in, where we buy our coffee, where our employees raise their families. That's the standard our work gets judged against, and the reason we'll usually pick up the phone when a client from 2009 calls because a hinge needs adjusting. When scheduling allows, we also try to take on a project at cost each year for a local family who needs it.

If you’re looking for a contractor who combines expert craftsmanship with excellent project management and communication, I would highly recommend JDI Construction and Remodeling. We wouldn’t hesitate to work with them again.

Portland, OR · Sep 2026

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

HOW WE WORK
Our 3-Step Remodeling Process

We manage all aspects of your project, ensuring clear updates and high-quality results from beginning to end. The JDI approach.

3
steps from call to completion
1
dedicated project manager
5-yr
written workmanship warranty
Get started
Call (360) 844-3234 →
01
Get in Touch

Reach out to us online or give us a call to schedule your free consultation. Our team is here to discuss your home remodeling needs and give you all the information you need.

Personal Consultation

Meet with our dedicated renovation expert in person to discuss your ideas. We'll visit your home to understand your needs and offer expert advice.

What to Expect

During your consultation, we'll engage in a thorough discussion to ensure we address all your concerns and goals. We'll cover:

Your vision
Budget
Timeline
Design ideas
Project goals
Detailed Estimate

Whether you have a design ready or are working with a designer, we'll provide a detailed estimate for your project. We collaborate with your chosen professionals to ensure a smooth remodel, giving you a clear view of costs and timelines.

Free Consultation
02
Kickoff the Design Phase

Once you sign the design agreement, our design team will meet with you to discuss your priorities, goals, and design style for your home remodel project.

In-Depth Design Consultation

We will discuss your personal design style and create renders, select finishes, and visit partner showrooms for materials and fixtures to ensure the perfect match.

Design Development

During the design process, we'll work closely with you to ensure your vision is brought to life. Our team will maintain open communication, providing regular updates and seeking your input at every stage. You can expect:

Thorough layout plans
Custom design options
Selection of finishes
3D design renders
Detailed mood boards
Design Finalization & Budget

After all design choices are made, we ensure everything is within budget, order materials, and schedule the construction phase, including the permit process.

03
Start Your Project

We'll kick off with a pre-construction meeting to outline logistics and expectations. Our design team hands over all details to the construction crew, and a dedicated project manager becomes your main point of contact.

Portal Access for Updates

You can check our client portal for instant updates on your project, as well as access to invoices, progress photos, and daily reports. This way, you'll be fully informed during every step of the process.

Construction Phase Coordination

During the construction phase, let us take the stress out of your project from start to finish. Our goal is to ensure a smooth, hassle-free experience with seamless collaboration between design and construction teams.

Coordinate all contractors
Schedule city inspections
Manage material vendors
Ensure smooth workflow
Align with your design vision
Final Walkthrough

When we're done, we'll do a final walkthrough to ensure everything meets your expectations. We'll provide documentation of installed products, vendor warranties, product packets, and our 5-year warranty. We want to deliver a project you'll be proud of!

HOW WE STAND BEHIND THE WORK
What every JDI project comes with.
1
Written, line-item estimates
A signed estimate before work begins, so the scope and the price are on paper.
See our process →
2
A dedicated project manager
One point of contact, with portal access for updates through the build.
How projects run →
3
Design and build under one roof
The people designing your layout are the people accountable for building it.
About design-build →
4
Permits handled for you
We pull the permits the work requires in Vancouver, Portland, Clark County, and Multnomah County.
See our process →
5
5-year workmanship warranty
Written, and backed by the same local team years after the project wraps.
Read the warranty →
6
Financing available
Through our lending partners, Lend Home Improvements and Medallion Bank. Subject to credit approval.
Financing options →

At JDI Construction, we believe exceptional remodeling begins with exceptional people. Portland, OR · Sep 2026

★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

JDI Construction NW LLC is a design-build remodeler based at 1419 Broadway Street in Vancouver, Washington. Since 2007 we have completed 500+ projects across Clark County and the Portland metro: kitchens, bathrooms, whole-home remodels, additions, ADUs and exterior work.

Design and construction stay with one company. A designer plans the space with you, you approve a written, itemized estimate, and a dedicated project manager runs the build, pulls the permits and coordinates every trade until the final walkthrough.

What does a remodel cost in Vancouver and Portland?
QUICK ANSWER

In 2026, JDI design-build kitchens start at about $28,000, bathrooms at about $9,000 and whole-home remodels at about $85,000 in the Portland–Vancouver metro. Those prices include design, permits, labor and finished materials. Your firm price comes in writing after a free in-home visit.

See your own range in 90 seconds: kitchen, bathroom or whole-home calculator.

What moves the price most
Finish level

The biggest single driver. A Signature finish package typically runs about 1.6× an Essential one for the same room.

Layout & structure

Moving walls, plumbing or gas, a larger island, and custom cabinetry add the most after finishes.

Scope & phasing

One room, several rooms, or the whole house. Phasing spreads the cost but adds about 5–10% over one continuous build.

How long does a remodel take?

On-site time after design and permits are done. Your written proposal includes your own schedule.

PROJECT	TYPICAL ON-SITE TIME
Bathroom	4–6 weeks; primary suites 6–10 weeks
Kitchen	About 3 weeks (refresh) to 5–8 weeks (full gut); cabinet delivery sets the start
Whole home	4–7 months; 7–14 months with additions

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Planning a kitchen that earns its keep in Vancouver

A kitchen remodel is really a sequence of decisions, and the order you make them in is what keeps the budget and the timeline on track. JDI Construction is a family-owned, Vancouver-based design-build remodeler, and a kitchen is the most complex room we build — cabinets, counters, appliances, plumbing, electrical, and often a wall or two, all landing on one schedule. This is home turf for us: we're headquartered right here in Clark County, and we've remodeled kitchens in neighborhoods from the older streets near Hough and Shumway to the newer subdivisions out past Cascade Park.

Because our designers and installers work as one team, the kitchen you approve is the kitchen that gets built. We don't draw a plan and then hand it off to a separate contractor and hope everything translates on site — the people designing your layout are the people accountable for making it real.

The parts that matter most

A kitchen has to look right, but it has to work first. These are the details that decide whether it does, and where experience shows:

1
Layout
The work triangle — sink, range, refrigerator — decides whether cooking feels natural or cramped.
2
Cabinets & storage
The longest lead item and the biggest line; drawers and a pantry planned around how you actually cook.
3
Counters
Durable work surfaces with enough uninterrupted run to prep, plus the template-to-install gap worth planning for.
4
Lighting
Task light over the counters and island, not a single fixture in the middle of the ceiling.
A few decisions worth making early

The choices that swing a kitchen's budget and schedule are the ones best settled before anyone swings a hammer. Chief among them is whether to open a wall to the dining or living room — a frequent request in Vancouver's older Hough and Shumway-era homes, where the kitchen was built as a closed box — and that hinges entirely on whether the wall carries load. Then there's the island: it only earns its place if you have the room for 36 to 42 inches of clear walkway on every side you'll actually use. We also decide early whether to keep the current layout or move the sink, range, or refrigerator, because relocating plumbing, gas lines, or the vent run is where cost quietly accumulates. Finally, we lock the cabinet style up front — cabinets are the longest lead item, and their delivery date sets the entire schedule, so a late decision there pushes everything behind it.

What Vancouver kitchens tend to need

Vancouver has an unusually wide range of housing, and the kitchens split along it. In the established neighborhoods closer to the river and downtown, homes tend to have compact, closed-off kitchens — a galley or a single walled run built for a different era of cooking. Opening those up almost always turns up dated wiring and undersized plumbing that has to be brought current before the new kitchen goes in, so we plan for it rather than discover it mid-project.

Out in the newer parts of east Vancouver and around Cascade Park, the footprint is usually there but the kitchen is builder-grade — stock cabinets, a token island, and never enough storage for the size of the room. There the work is upgrading finishes, rethinking the island and the flow, and adding the deep-drawer and pantry storage that make a big kitchen function. Either way, we settle the electrical and venting before cabinets arrive, since those are the expensive things to fix afterward.

What does a kitchen remodel cost in Vancouver?

Short answer: JDI's published planning ranges are $28,000-$45,000 to $85,000-$130,000 for a small kitchen (under 120 sq ft), $42,000-$65,000 to $130,000-$210,000 for a medium kitchen (120 to 200 sq ft) and $62,000-$95,000 to $210,000-$360,000 for a large kitchen (over 200 sq ft), from our Essential to our Luxury tier, before any sales tax. They are planning ranges, not quotes; the kitchen cost calculator narrows yours by size and finish level.

What a Vancouver kitchen costs comes down to a handful of big levers rather than the address on the door. Cabinets are usually the largest single line, and the jump from stock to semi-custom to fully custom moves the number more than any other choice you'll make. After that it's the countertop material, whether you're relocating plumbing, gas, or walls, the level of appliances you choose, and simply the size of the room. Keeping the existing layout and replacing cabinets and counters sits at one end of the range; a full gut with a new island, moved plumbing, and an opened-up wall sits at the other. Because our design and our trades are both in-house, we can steer the plan toward what matters to you and pull back where it doesn't — and you get an itemized estimate once the kitchen is drawn, so every choice shows what it adds.

How long does a kitchen remodel take?

Short answer: at JDI, the construction phase typically takes about 3 weeks for a cosmetic refresh, about 5 weeks for a pull-and-replace in the same layout and 5 to 8 weeks for a full gut. Design, ordering and permits come first. See each step and who you meet.

Plan on several weeks of on-site work for most kitchens, but the clock really starts before demolition: cabinets are the longest lead item, and their delivery date drives everything, so we order them the moment the design is locked. Opening a wall, moving plumbing, or upgrading an older electrical panel adds time, and the century-old homes near the river occasionally hand us a surprise behind the plaster. We give you a realistic schedule up front, pull the permits the work requires, and sequence the trades so you keep a working kitchen for as much of the project as we can manage.

Why homeowners in Vancouver choose JDI

Design-build means one team owns the whole kitchen — the layout, the cabinets, the counters, the plumbing, and the electrical — so your plan is never drawn by one company and handed to trades who never saw it drawn. We pull the permits, coordinate every trade so the tile setter isn't idle waiting on the electrician, keep you current through our client portal, and stand behind the finished work with a five-year workmanship warranty. Being based right here in Vancouver, we're a short drive from your door, which makes us easy to reach both during the project and years after it wraps.

Where a shower earns its keep

Whether you are converting a tub or rebuilding a leaking shower, the work that matters happens before the first tile goes up. JDI Construction is a family-owned, Vancouver-based design-build remodeler, and we build a shower from the framing out — the membrane, the pan, and the slope first, then the tile and glass you actually see. Get that hidden work right and a shower holds up for decades; skip it and the leak surfaces long after the tile looked finished. Vancouver is home for us, and we've rebuilt showers in nearly every kind of house Clark County has — from the older Hough and Shumway neighborhoods to the newer subdivisions out past Cascade Park.

Because our designers and our installers are the same team, the shower you sign off on is the shower we build — we don't pass a finished set of plans to an outside contractor and cross our fingers that the waterproofing gets detailed correctly. Below is how we think a shower through, what tends to turn up in Vancouver homes, and what to expect on cost and timeline.

The details that decide how it holds up

A shower can look flawless and still fail, because the parts that keep it dry are the ones you can't see once the tile is set. These are the details we get right first:

1
Slope to drain
Every surface pitched so water always finds the drain, not the grout lines.
2
Tile & grout
Beautiful, but it's the surface — what's waterproofed behind it does the real work.
3
Sealing the seams
Corners, the curb, and the drain flange are where leaks start, so they're detailed carefully.
4
Accessibility
Grab-bar blocking, a bench, and a low or zero threshold if you're planning to age in place.
A few decisions worth making early

The choices that shape a shower's cost and layout are the ones best settled before demolition. The big one is whether to turn a tub into a walk-in shower — a smart move when the tub sits unused, though we usually advise keeping at least one tub somewhere in the house for resale. Next is curbed versus curbless: a zero-threshold shower is cleaner to look at and easier to walk into, but it depends on recessed framing and an exact slope, so it has to be planned, not improvised. Then there are the extras that must be framed in from the start rather than tacked on later — a bench, recessed niches, a second showerhead, or blocking for grab bars. We also lock in the glass and the drain early, because both change how the pan and walls get built.

What Vancouver showers tend to need

In the older parts of Vancouver — the Hough and Shumway-era homes near downtown and the streets around them — we most often tear out a tired tiled shower that has started to leak, or a dated fiberglass insert that's outlived its usefulness. The honest fix in those houses is rebuilding the waterproofing behind the tile, not re-tiling over a pan that never drained right in the first place. Opening the walls is the moment to correct all of that.

Out in east Vancouver and around Cascade Park, the newer construction usually came with a builder-grade shower — sound but plain, with a small pan, a plastic surround, and a low-end door. There the work is an upgrade: a tiled walk-in, better frameless or semi-frameless glass, and the niche and slope details that make it feel custom instead of standard. Either way, given how wet the Columbia River corridor stays, we treat the membrane and the ventilation as the parts we never shortcut — that's what protects everything else.

What does a shower remodel cost in Vancouver?

What a shower costs in Vancouver comes down to what you're building, not the neighborhood. Swapping one prefab insert for another sits at the low end; a fully tiled, curbless walk-in with frameless glass and a linear drain sits at the other. The levers in between are size, tile versus a prefab pan, whether the drain has to move, the glass you choose, and the waterproofing system behind all of it. Curbless runs higher because the framing and slope take more labor to get exactly right. Since our design and our trades are both in-house, we can steer the plan toward what you care about most — and you get an itemized estimate after we've seen the space, so the number reflects your shower rather than an average off a chart.

How long does a shower remodel take?

A shower-only remodel usually moves faster than a full bathroom, but it's not a weekend project. Waterproofing and mortar need time to cure before any tile goes on, and the tile and grout need their own set and cure time before the shower can be used again. Moving the drain, going curbless, or opening walls in an older Vancouver home all add days. We hand you a realistic schedule before demolition starts, pull the permits the work requires, and sequence things so you're not left without a working shower any longer than necessary.

Why homeowners in Vancouver choose JDI

Design-build means one team is accountable for the entire shower — the framing, the waterproofing, the pan, the tile, and the glass — so the part that matters most never gets quietly subcontracted to whoever bids lowest. We pull the permits, coordinate the trades, keep you updated through our client portal, and back the work with a five-year workmanship warranty. Because we're based right here in Vancouver, we're close enough to be responsive during the project and years down the road. Financing is available through Lend Home Improvement with $0 down and no prepayment penalty, and every consultation includes a free 3D design layout.

Whole House Design, Remodeling and Renovation

Every whole-home remodel starts with how you want to live in the house. We plan the layout, the systems and the finishes as one project, then build it with one team from design to the final walkthrough

Tap images to enlarge

Remodeling a whole house, planned as one project

The biggest question in a whole-house remodel usually isn't the finishes — it's whether to live through it or move out while we work. JDI Construction is a family-owned, Vancouver-based design-build remodeler, and we treat a project this size as what it really is: a series of connected projects run on one schedule, under one design vision, by one team that answers for the layout, the systems behind the walls, and every finish. It's also the one moment when it's genuinely efficient to fix the bones of the house — the electrical panel, the plumbing, the insulation — all while the walls are already open. In Vancouver that matters, because the Clark County seat holds everything from older Hough and Shumway-era homes near the core to newer construction out in Cascade Park and east Vancouver, and each asks for a different plan.

Because our designers and our installers are one team, the home you sign off on in the drawings is the home that actually gets built. We don't hand a plan set to a separate contractor and hope the pieces line up on site. Here's what a whole-house project covers, what tends to surface in Vancouver homes, and what to expect on cost and timeline.

The parts that matter most

Some of the most important work in a whole-house remodel never shows up in a photo. These are the pieces we plan first, because they're what the finished home rests on:

1
The invisible layer
Wiring, plumbing, HVAC, and insulation — the upgrades that are cheap now and expensive later.
2
Permits & structure
Structural changes and system upgrades pulled and inspected, handled for you.
3
Cohesion
Materials and details repeated across rooms so nothing looks added on.
4
Project management
One team and one schedule coordinating every trade from start to finish.
A few decisions worth making early

The choices that set a whole-house budget and schedule are best settled before anyone swings a hammer. The first is whether you'll live through it or move out — staying put keeps costs down but means living around active work, and we sequence the job to keep parts of the house usable either way. From there: how much of the layout and structure you want to change, since moving or removing walls opens a home up but brings engineering and load-path work with it; which systems to fold in now, because re-piping, rewiring, upgrading the panel, or swapping out HVAC is far cheaper while the walls are open than as a separate trip back later; and whether to tackle everything at once or phase it over time. We put these trade-offs on the table early so the plan fits both how you live and what you intend to spend.

What Vancouver whole-house projects tend to involve

In the older neighborhoods closer to central Vancouver — the Hough and Shumway-era streets and the homes that grew up around them — a whole-house remodel usually means opening up a chopped-up original floor plan and dragging the mechanicals into the present. Knob-and-tube wiring, undersized and crowded panels, galvanized or aging supply lines, and thin attic insulation all get addressed while the walls are open, so the house keeps its character but finally performs like a modern one.

Out in east Vancouver and around Cascade Park, the newer and larger homes are more often about reconfiguring for the way a household actually lives now — reworking an entire level, and replacing builder-grade finishes throughout so the kitchen, primary suite, and living spaces read as one cohesive design rather than a series of separate updates. Either way, in the damp Pacific Northwest we fold insulation, moisture control, and ventilation into the scope, because a whole-house project is the right time to get them right.

What does a whole-house remodel cost in Vancouver?

Whole-house cost is driven by scope before anything else: how many rooms are in play, how much of the layout and structure changes, and which systems you update along the way. Square footage matters, but so does the age of the home — an older home near central Vancouver is more likely to turn up wiring, plumbing, or framing that should be corrected while the walls are open, which is precisely why we carry a contingency in the budget for hidden conditions. Finish level is the other major lever, from clean and durable to fully custom throughout. Because our design and our trades are both in-house, we can plan the entire project against one realistic number and show you where each decision lands, instead of pricing it piecemeal after the fact.

How long does a whole-house remodel take?

A whole-house remodel is measured in months, not weeks, and the timeline follows scope, structural work, and how much of the home is touched at once. We give you a realistic schedule before demolition, pull and coordinate the permits the work requires, and run the trades in the order they have to go — demo, then structural, then rough-ins, insulation, drywall, and finally finishes. Where it makes sense, we phase the work so you can keep living in part of the home while the rest is underway.

Why homeowners in Vancouver choose JDI

A whole-house remodel has more moving parts than any other project, which is exactly why design-build fits it so well: one team owns the design, the structure, the systems, and the finishes, so nothing slips through the gaps between separate companies. We handle the permitting, coordinate every trade against a single schedule, keep you updated through our client portal, and back the work with a five-year workmanship warranty. Based right here in Vancouver, we're close enough to be on-site and responsive across a project of this length — which, on a job that runs for months, is worth more than it sounds.

EXTERIOR REMODELING · PORTLAND & VANCOUVER
Exterior Remodeling in Portland & Vancouver

In a climate this wet, your home's exterior is a rain-management system first and a source of curb appeal second. Between the fall and spring, the Portland metro and Clark County take on the better part of forty inches of rain, most of it as a slow, sideways drizzle that finds every unsealed seam. Get the water out and everything else — the color, the trim, the front door — is finish work on a house that will last.

Water is the enemy. Every exterior decision we make at JDI Construction starts from that fact and works outward.

We've been remodeling exteriors across Portland, Vancouver, and the surrounding SW Washington towns since 2007, on everything from mid-century ranches to century-old foursquares in older neighborhoods. What follows isn't a menu of siding options — it's how the envelope actually keeps a Pacific Northwest home dry, where that system tends to fail, and how we rebuild it so it stops failing.

The envelope, layer by layer

It's tempting to think of siding as the wall, but siding is only the outermost layer of a system that manages water. Rain gets behind cladding on every house — that's expected, not a defect — so the real job is giving that water a fast, uninterrupted path back out before it reaches the wood and insulation underneath.

Behind the siding sits a weather-resistive barrier, the house wrap that sheds bulk water down and away from the sheathing while still letting the wall breathe. At every opening and transition, flashing hands water from one layer to the next: over windows and doors, at the base of walls, where a roof meets a wall, and around every pipe and vent that punches through. Windows and doors are engineered holes in that barrier, so how they're integrated with the wrap and flashing matters more than the units themselves. Trim caps the edges and joints where two materials meet. And above it all, the roofline, gutters, and downspouts are supposed to catch the largest volume of water and carry it clear of the walls and foundation entirely.

When one layer is skipped or lapped the wrong way — house wrap tucked behind flashing instead of over it, a gutter dumping against a wall, trim with an open top edge — water stops draining and starts collecting. That's how a small detail becomes rot inside the wall you can't see. We treat the exterior as the single connected system it is, because that's the only way it holds up here.

Choosing siding for a wet climate

Siding is the decision most homeowners lead with, and in the Northwest the right answer is driven as much by moisture performance as by looks. The four materials below cover the vast majority of what we install. There's no single winner — the best choice depends on your home's style, your appetite for maintenance, and your budget.

Material	Look	Moisture performance	Maintenance	Relative cost
Fiber cement	Crisp, painted-wood look with clean lines; broad range of profiles and colors.	Excellent — won't rot, swell, or feed mold, and stands up well to constant damp.	Low; occasional repaint and caulk checks. Dimensionally stable in wet weather.	Mid to upper-mid
Engineered wood	Warm, natural wood-grain appearance; lighter and easier to handle than fiber cement.	Very good when properly sealed and flashed; treated to resist moisture, but edges and cuts must be sealed.	Low to moderate; periodic repaint and inspection of field-cut edges.	Mid
Cedar / real wood	The genuine article — rich grain and depth that ages beautifully; ideal for period and craftsman homes.	Naturally rot-resistant but the most demanding in wet climates; needs meticulous detailing and a maintained finish.	High; regular staining or sealing every few years to keep water out.	Upper-mid to high
Vinyl	Uniform, simple look; wide color range, though profiles read less substantial up close.	Good — impervious to water itself, but relies on the wrap and flashing behind it, since it isn't a sealed surface.	Very low; rinse occasionally, no painting required.	Lower

Whatever the cladding, its moisture performance is only as good as the barrier and flashing behind it — which is exactly why we spend as much time on what you can't see as on what you can.

Where water actually gets in

Rot almost never starts in the open field of a wall. It starts at the transitions — the handful of spots where the drainage plane is interrupted and one material meets another. These are the details we inspect first and build most carefully, because getting them right is the entire difference between a wall that dries and a wall that stays wet.

Window & door head and pan flashing
Every opening needs flashing over the top (the head) to divert water down and out, and a sloped pan beneath the sill to catch anything that gets past it. A missing or reversed pan is one of the most common causes of hidden rot below Northwest windows.
Kickout flashing at roof-wall intersections
Where a roof edge dies into a wall, a small kickout piece diverts the concentrated runoff away from the siding. Leave it out and a firehose of roof water runs straight down inside the wall — a classic source of rot behind the cladding on multi-story homes.
Deck ledger flashing
The board that attaches a deck to the house is a horizontal shelf bolted through the siding. Without proper flashing above and behind it, water sits at that connection and rots both the ledger and the framing it's fastened to — a structural failure, not just a cosmetic one.
Penetrations
Every hose bib, dryer vent, electrical box, and light fixture is a hole in the drainage plane. Each one needs to be integrated into the house wrap and sealed so water is directed around it, not funneled behind it.
Gutters, downspouts, and grading
The system's first line of defense handles the most water. Undersized or clogged gutters overflow onto walls; downspouts that discharge at the foundation drive water back toward the crawlspace. We check that runoff is carried well clear of the house and that the ground slopes away from it.
Windows & doors

Windows and doors do double duty — they're where the most heat escapes and where water most often sneaks in, so we treat them as an energy upgrade and a waterproofing detail at the same time. In older Portland and Vancouver homes, we frequently open a wall for re-siding and find soft, rotted framing beneath a window that's been quietly leaking for years; catching and repairing that rot is part of doing the job right, not an upsell we hope you won't notice.

New units are only as watertight as their installation. We integrate each window and door with the house wrap and set it on proper pan flashing so any water that reaches the sill drains back to the exterior rather than into the wall. Modern insulated glass cuts drafts and condensation, which matters through a long, damp winter. And because so many homes here have a distinct architectural character, we match the sightlines, grille pattern, and proportions to the house — so a rot repair or an efficiency upgrade reads as original, not like a patch.

Curb appeal that also protects

Once the envelope is sound, the visible choices are where a house finally looks transformed — and the good news is that nearly every one of them is doing protective work, too. Fresh trim isn't only a crisp line around a window; it's the cap that keeps water out of the joint. A quality exterior paint or factory finish isn't just a color; it's the coating that shields the siding from constant moisture and UV. A new front door resets the whole face of the house while sealing one of its largest openings.

Mixing materials — a band of shingle-style siding on a gable, a stone or panel accent at the entry, a contrasting trim color — adds the kind of depth and craftsmanship that make a home stand out on the street, provided it's done with restraint and true to the home's era. That combination of a weather-tight envelope and a considered exterior is also what protects your investment: a home that clearly sheds water and presents well holds its value and its appeal in a way that a fresh coat of paint over hidden problems never will.

Exterior questions we hear most

What's the best siding for Oregon rain?

Fiber cement is the workhorse in our climate — it won't rot, swell, or feed mold, and it holds paint well through wet winters. Engineered wood is a strong lighter-weight option, and cedar is beautiful for period homes if you'll keep up the finish. But the honest answer is that any of them performs well over a correctly built barrier and flashing, and fails without one. The material matters; what's behind it matters more.

Should I repaint or re-side?

If the siding is sound and just tired, paint is the smart, affordable move. Re-siding makes sense when you're seeing cracked or cupping boards, soft spots, paint that won't hold, or repeated moisture issues — signs the cladding or what's behind it is failing. We'll open a section and tell you honestly which one you're looking at rather than talk you into the bigger job.

Can you work on the exterior in winter?

Yes — we work through the Northwest wet season year-round. We sequence around the weather, keep walls protected and dried-in as we go, and never leave sheathing exposed to the rain. Some finishes, like certain paints, need dry, mild windows to cure properly, so we schedule those steps for the right conditions. The structural and weatherproofing work carries on regardless.

Will you match my existing siding?

When we're repairing or extending rather than replacing everything, yes — we work to match the profile, exposure, and color as closely as the material allows so the repair blends in. On older homes with discontinued products, a perfect match isn't always possible; in those cases we'll walk you through the closest options and where a seam will fall before we start.

Start with a free exterior walkthrough

We'll walk the outside of your home with you, point out where water is getting in — the flashing, the gutters, the tired siding — and lay out what it takes to make the envelope watertight and the exterior look like new. It's an honest, no-pressure assessment, and it's free.

Design-Build Contractor in Portland & Vancouver

Most remodeling problems are not construction problems. They are handoff problems — the gap that opens when the person who drew your plans is not the person who has to build them. In the traditional model, that gap is where budgets blow up, timelines slip, and "not my job" gets said out loud. Design-build closes it by putting design and construction under one roof, on one contract, answerable to one team. When something goes sideways, there is no one to point at but us — and that is exactly the point.

JDI Construction has worked this way since 2007. We design in-house, price as we design, and build with our own trades and project managers across the Portland OR metro, Vancouver WA, and Clark County. You are never the messenger carrying drawings between an architect who has moved on and a contractor seeing them for the first time. One team owns the outcome from the first sketch to the final walkthrough.

Design-build vs. the traditional way

The difference is not a matter of taste. It changes who is accountable, when you learn what things cost, and who absorbs the surprises. Here is the same remodel, run two ways.

THE TRADITIONAL PATH
Design-bid-build
THE SETUP
Hire an architect or designer, complete drawings, then send them out to bid among separate general contractors.
ACCOUNTABILITY
Split. The designer blames the builder, the builder blames the drawings, and you sit in the middle mediating.
BUDGET ALIGNMENT
You learn the real price only after design is finished — often to discover the plans cost far more than you can spend.
TIMELINE
Sequential. Design fully wraps, then bidding, then a new team ramps up on plans they have never seen.
CHANGE ORDERS
Frequent. Gaps and conflicts in the drawings surface mid-build, when changes are most expensive.
WHO OWNS PROBLEMS
You do. Coordinating two parties who never chose to work together becomes your part-time job.
THE JDI WAY
Design-build
THE SETUP
One team designs and builds under a single contract. Designers, estimators, and project managers sit at the same table from day one.
ACCOUNTABILITY
Single. One company is responsible for the design working, the build matching it, and the result lasting.
BUDGET ALIGNMENT
Continuous. Real pricing is developed alongside the design, so the plan and the budget move together — never apart.
TIMELINE
Overlapping. Design and preconstruction advance in parallel, and the crew that builds already knows the plan.
CHANGE ORDERS
Fewer by design. Constructability is checked while drawings are still being made, not after the walls open.
WHO OWNS PROBLEMS
We do. Coordination happens inside our own company — you approve decisions instead of refereeing them.
How our design-build process works

Because design and pricing live in the same building, they do not take turns — they run side by side. The middle of this process is deliberately parallel: as the design develops, the numbers develop with it, so nothing gets drawn that we haven't already priced.

1. Discovery & budget

We start with how you actually live in the space, the scope you have in mind, and an honest working budget. This sets the guardrails before a single line is drawn.

2. Design and pricing, developed in parallel
DESIGN TRACK

Our in-house designers develop layouts, selections, and drawings — iterating with your feedback toward a plan you love.

PRICING TRACK

At the same time, our estimators price each decision in real time, flagging cost drivers and suggesting alternatives before drawings are finalized.

↓ THE TWO TRACKS STAY IN SYNC ↓
3. One fixed proposal

The two tracks converge into a single proposal: a design you have approved and a price built from it, not guessed at around it. No mystery allowances hiding the real number.

4. Build with the same crew

Our own trades and project managers execute the plan they helped shape. The people building your project already understand the intent behind every detail — nothing gets lost in translation.

5. Warranty

We stand behind the finished work with a 5-year workmanship warranty — the same company that designed and built it answers for it afterward.

Why one contract saves money — not just time

People assume design-build is simply faster. It is — but the bigger savings come from the money you never spend. When pricing runs alongside design, value engineering happens where it belongs: on paper, early, while options are still cheap to explore. If a wall move triples the plumbing cost, you find out during design and decide whether it is worth it — not after the drywall is up and the only choices left are expensive ones.

That feedback loop is impossible in the traditional model, where the price arrives only after the design is locked. In design-build, our estimators are in the room as decisions are made, so the design is shaped by what it costs to build. Materials get compared, structural choices get pressure-tested, and trade-offs get made with real numbers in front of you.

The result is far fewer surprise change orders. Most change orders are not homeowners changing their minds — they are the plans and the field finally meeting and disagreeing. Because our builders review constructability while the drawings are still being made, those conflicts get caught before they become invoices. One contract means the incentive to draw something buildable and the responsibility to build it belong to the same company. That alignment is where the savings actually come from.

What it looks like day to day

Once the build begins, you work with one project manager — a single person who knows your project, holds the schedule, and is your point of contact from start to finish. You are not chasing a designer for one answer and a foreman for another. Questions have one address.

Progress lives in a client portal, so you can see the schedule, selections, approvals, and updates without waiting for a phone call to find out where things stand. Decisions are documented, so nothing important lives only in someone's memory.

And when the job is done, the same team that designed it and built it stands behind it — backed by our 5-year workmanship warranty. There is no handing you off to a warranty department that was not there for the work. The people who made the promises are the people who keep them. That continuity is not a perk of design-build; it is the whole reason the model exists.

Is design-build right for your project?
Where it shines

Complex or multi-room scope where design and construction have to be coordinated closely. Homeowners who want budget certainty before committing, and who would rather approve decisions than personally coordinate architects, trades, and suppliers. If "I just don't want to manage all of this" describes you, design-build was built for you.

An honest note

A very simple, well-defined project — a like-for-like swap with no design decisions and no unknowns — may not need the full design-build engine. If that is your situation, we will tell you plainly rather than sell you a process you do not need.

Design-build questions, answered
Q.What is design-build?

Design-build is a delivery model where a single company handles both the design and the construction of your remodel under one contract. Instead of hiring a designer and then hiring a separate contractor, you work with one team that is accountable for the whole project — from the first concept through the final walkthrough.

Q.Is design-build more expensive?

Usually the opposite. Because pricing is developed alongside the design, expensive surprises get caught on paper instead of mid-build, and value engineering happens while changes are still cheap. Fewer change orders and less rework typically make design-build the more cost-controlled path — you trade the illusion of a low upfront bid for a real number you can plan around.

Q.Do you design first and price later?

No — that is the exact gap we are built to avoid. Design and pricing run in parallel. As our designers develop your plan, our estimators price each decision in real time, so the design and the budget stay aligned the whole way through rather than colliding at the end.

Q.Can I bring my own architect or existing plans?

Yes. If you already have drawings or an architect you want to keep, we can work from your plans and fold them into our build process. We will review them for constructability and pricing so you still get the budget alignment and single point of accountability that make design-build work.

Q.Who pulls the permits?

We do. As your licensed contractor — Oregon CCB #176101 and Washington #JDICOCN932KZ — we handle permitting and coordinate the required inspections as part of the project, so you are not navigating the jurisdiction on your own.

Book a design consultation

Bring us the space, the wish list, and the honest budget. In a design consultation we will walk your project, talk through what design-build can do for it, and show you how the plan and the price get built together — before you commit to anything. Built by family. Trusted by neighbors.

Mark Pavliuk

★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a great experience with JDI Construction.
Definitely a reputable team. Highly recommend them. They definitely know what they are doing. Also very knowledgeable. Thank you.
Mark Pavliuk
Portland, OR · Sep 2026
View on Google
★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

All-White Kitchen and Whole-Home Refresh in Vancouver, WA

This Vancouver, WA whole-home remodel by JDI Construction reworked the entry, stairs, living and family rooms, dining nook, and kitchen around a single clean palette — crisp white shaker cabinetry, stainless appliances, white subway tile, marble-look quartz, and a quiet brushed nickel hardware story that runs from room to room.

The kitchen pairs floor-to-ceiling white shaker perimeter cabinetry with a matching white center island, both finished in the same satin paint. Brushed nickel slim bar pulls run consistently across every door and drawer, and glass-front upper cabinets above the cooking wall add visual depth without breaking the all-white palette. A coffee station tucks off to one side with its own counter run and beverage fridge.

White marble-look quartz countertops cap the cabinetry, and a classic white subway tile backsplash in an offset pattern keeps the wall surfaces quiet. A stainless slide-in gas range sits under a stainless chimney hood, with a built-in stainless double wall oven and microwave tower next to a counter-depth French-door refrigerator completing the appliance run. Vintage industrial sconces with white glass globes line up over the sink and run of windows.

Beyond the kitchen, the entry, stairs, living and family rooms all carry the same crisp white-and-warm-wood palette — white walls, light oak hardwood floors, and quiet trim — keeping the home reading as a single coordinated design rather than a patchwork of separate scopes. The result is a whole-home remodel that uses one clean palette without ever feeling sterile.

Key Features
Custom white shaker cabinetry in kitchen, perimeter, and island
Glass-front upper cabinets and dedicated coffee station with beverage fridge
White marble-look quartz countertops
White subway tile backsplash in offset pattern
Stainless gas range, double wall oven tower, and French-door refrigerator
Vintage industrial sconce lighting over the sink wall
Light oak hardwood flooring through main living areas

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

11 Photos
Olive Green Kitchen and Modern Open-Tread Staircase Remodel in Camas, WA

JDI Construction reworked this Camas, WA home as a coordinated kitchen-and-staircase remodel — a confident olive-green shaker kitchen paired with a refreshed open-tread staircase that bridges the home's downstairs and upstairs in one consistent material register.

The kitchen pairs custom olive-green shaker cabinetry on every cabinet — perimeter, island, and tall pantry tower — against bright white quartz countertops, a white handmade-look subway tile backsplash, and slim brushed nickel bar pulls. A custom painted range hood with a stained wood band at the base anchors the cooking wall, and dark industrial-style pendants with brass interiors hang above the island.

Function shows up in the smaller decisions: an apron-front farmhouse sink, an under-counter beverage fridge, a stainless French-door refrigerator with water dispenser, a microwave drawer set into the cabinetry, and natural-stained floating walnut shelves at the sink wall that pull the home's warmer wood tone into the cooking zone.

The staircase carries the design upstairs with stained oak treads, white risers, an oak handrail and newel post, and a row of slim black-painted metal balusters that give the run a modern, almost industrial silhouette. The result is a kitchen and staircase remodel that bridges two distinct work scopes with one shared material story.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a great experience with JDI Construction.
Definitely a reputable team. Highly recommend them. They definitely know what they are doing. Also very knowledgeable. Thank you.
Mark Pavliuk
Portland, OR · Sep 2026
View on Google
★★★★★
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely Amazing Experience!
When we purchased our home in La Center, the downstairs only had two rooms and one bathroom. Upstairs had three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, and a mudroom. We knew we wanted to transform the downstairs into a comfortable living space for my mother-in-law, and finding the right contractor was extremely important to us.
That’s when we hired Art and his team, and honestly, we could not have asked for a better person to work with.
From our very first meeting, Art was friendly, patient, an incredible listener, and truly understood what we wanted. He took the time to sit down with us, go through the entire remodeling process, discuss the timeline and pricing, and answer all of our questions. We had multiple meetings throughout the project, and his communication and follow-up were outstanding.
His team did an amazing job. Everything downstairs was completely transformed. They remodeled the existing bathroom, added another beautiful bathroom with a gorgeous shower, relocated and redesigned the space to create a master-style room, and even added a full kitchen downstairs.
What started as a downstairs area became essentially an ADU for my mother-in-law. ❤️ It has made our family life so much easier. Grandma can comfortably have her own space downstairs while our family lives upstairs, but we are still all under one roof.
What impressed us most was how involved Art was throughout the entire process. He went with us to select tile and countertops, helped us make decisions, made sure the pricing was fair, and personally followed up to make sure everything was done correctly. Even after the project was completed, he continued checking in with Grandma to make sure she was doing well. His team has continued to be just as caring.
That level of care is something you don’t always find.
Our home is beautiful, completely remodeled, and feels brand new. More importantly, we’re grateful to have found someone who cared about our family—not just the project.
Art and his entire team, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We are truly thankful and blessed to have had you remodel our home. ❤️
If you are thinking about remodeling your home, I highly recommend giving Art and his team a call. You won’t just be hiring a contractor—you’ll be working with people who genuinely care about doing a great job and making sure you’re happy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Please consider JDI for your next project!
